newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIA PRODUCT SWAPS - SLIPS ON CRUDE FALLS.
newsitem.headline: ASIA PRODUCT SWAPS - SLIPS ON CRUDE FALLS.

text.p: Singapore oil product swaps were weaker at midday on Monday after significant falls to Friday's crude values, traders said.
But the fall in swaps values were small relative to the 42 cent per barrel drop in September Brent crude to $18.48 on the International Petroleum Exchange.
September gas oil was last quoted at $23.10/$23.25 per barrel, down from Friday's $23.25/$23.35. September traded earlier in the day at $23.08 and $23.10, brokers said.
Balance August was also quoted weaker as trading for the month wound down. It traded earlier in the day at $22.54 and the August/September spread was steady at minus 65 cents.
Traders said the smaller fall in gas oil values was partly due to the emergence of buying interest from Chinese trading companies.
But the purchases from these companies are not a signal of their return to the physical market, they said.
In the physical market on Friday, a European major sold to a Dutch trader 240,000 barrels for lifting Aug 23-27 at $22.40, down a hefty 68 cents from the previous trade on Wednesday.
September naphtha was last quoted at $21.20/$21.35 per barrel, down from Friday's $21.30/$21.55, brokers said.
Fuel oil edged down slightly as the market looked to strong bunker demand to keep prices steady.
September were last quoted at $102.00/$103.00, down slightly from Friday's $102.25/$103.00, they said.
